_note: Terms of art, one sentence each. The first use of a term on a sheet gets a dotted underline; a tap shows the sentence. `match` lists the forms that count. `notBefore` / `notAfter` list words that rule a use out ("in confidence", "independent shops"). Order matters: a term earlier in the list is looked for first.

terms.label: Whipped vote
terms.text: The party has decided how its members vote on this one, and breaking with it has a cost.

terms.label: Free vote
terms.text: The party takes no line, and each member votes as they see fit.

terms.label: The whip
terms.text: The member who counts the party's votes, makes sure everyone turns up, and leans on anyone who might not vote the line.

terms.label: The line
terms.text: The way the party wants its members to vote: yea, nay, or free.

terms.label: Pairing
terms.text: A member on each side agrees to sit out the same vote, so an absence costs neither side.

terms.label: Division
terms.text: A recorded vote: the bells ring, members file in, and every name is counted.

terms.label: The bells
terms.text: They ring across the Hill when a vote is called; members have minutes to reach the chamber before the doors close.

terms.label: Lobby
terms.text: The two sides members file into to be counted, yea or nay.

terms.label: Second reading
terms.text: The vote on a bill's principle, before committee goes through the detail.

terms.label: Committee
terms.text: Where a bill is gone through clause by clause and amended, between second and third reading.

terms.label: Third reading
terms.text: The last vote on a bill in the House, once committee has finished with it.

terms.label: Confidence
terms.text: Lose a confidence vote and the government falls, which means an election.

terms.label: Address in Reply
terms.text: The House's answer to the Throne Speech, and the first confidence vote of a Parliament.

terms.label: Throne Speech
terms.text: Opens a Parliament with the government's plan; the vote on it is the Address in Reply.

terms.label: The Speaker
terms.text: Chairs the House, keeps order, and votes only to break a tie.

terms.label: Question Period
terms.text: The daily hour when the opposition puts questions to ministers, with the cameras on.

terms.label: Order Paper
terms.text: The House's agenda: the business and the votes to come.

terms.label: Backbench
terms.text: Members with no job in cabinet or on the party's front rank. Everyone starts here.

terms.label: Front bench
terms.text: Ministers and their opposite numbers, who sit at the front and speak for the party.

terms.label: House leader
terms.text: Runs the party's business in the chamber: what comes up, and when.

terms.label: Parliamentary secretary
terms.text: A minister's helper from the backbench; the first rung up.

terms.label: Private member's bill
terms.text: A bill from a backbencher rather than the government, drawn by lottery for a rare slot.

terms.label: Opposition motion
terms.text: A day the opposition sets the business and puts its own motion to a vote.

terms.label: Caucus
terms.text: All of a party's members, meeting behind closed doors to settle the line and air grievances.

terms.label: Riding
terms.text: The constituency a member represents, and the people who can vote them out.

terms.label: By-election
terms.text: A vote in a single riding to fill a seat that has come empty mid-Parliament.

terms.label: Nomination
terms.text: The local party's choice of candidate; lose it and you don't run again under the banner.

terms.label: Crossing the floor
terms.text: Leaving your party to sit with another, or on your own, without an election.

terms.label: Independent
terms.text: A member who sits with no party: no whip, no caucus, and no one to count them.
